:::{#def-continuous-several}
#### Continuity in several variables

A real-valued function $f$ of a $p \times 1$ vector is **continuous at** $\vx$
if for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a $\delta > 0$ such that
$\abs{f(\vy) - f(\vx)} < \varepsilon$ whenever $\norm{\vy - \vx} < \delta$.
It is **continuous on** a set if it is continuous at every point of the set.
For $p = 1$, $\norm{\vy - \vx} = \abs{y - x}$,
and this is the usual [continuity](calculus.qmd#def-continuous).
A composition of continuous functions is continuous:
choose the $\delta$ for the outer function first,
and use it as the $\varepsilon$ for the inner one.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-continuous-several}
#### A continuous function, and a discontinuous one

- $f(\vx) = x_1 + x_2$ is continuous at every $\vx$.
  Each $\abs{y_i - x_i} \le \norm{\vy - \vx}$, since the squared length is a sum of nonnegative squares, so

  $$
  \ba
  \abs{f(\vy) - f(\vx)}
  &= \abs{(y_1 - x_1) + (y_2 - x_2)}
  && \text{(subtract)}
  \\
  &\le \abs{y_1 - x_1} + \abs{y_2 - x_2}
  && \text{(triangle inequality for numbers)}
  \\
  &\le 2\,\norm{\vy - \vx},
  && \text{(each term is at most } \norm{\vy - \vx} \text{)}
  \ea
  $$

  which is less than $\varepsilon$ whenever $\norm{\vy - \vx} < \delta = \varepsilon / 2$.
- $f(\vx) = 1$ if $x_1 > 0$ and $f(\vx) = 0$ otherwise is not continuous at $\vzero$:
  for $\varepsilon = \tfrac{1}{2}$ and any $\delta > 0$, the point $\vy = \tp{(\delta / 2, 0)}$
  has $\norm{\vy - \vzero} = \delta / 2 < \delta$ but $\abs{f(\vy) - f(\vzero)} = 1 > \tfrac{1}{2}$.

:::
